text:
alex_m: Quick heads-up — ran schema-fuzz structured-output tests across FP16 baseline, GPTQ-INT8, AWQ-4bit, and FP8 on model-x. Seeing JSON validity drop on function-calling/tool-args for quantized variants. :eyes:

priya_r: Ugh, how much of a drop? can you paste a failing example?

alex_m: Overall JSON-valid-rate (strict schema check): FP16 baseline = 99.6%, GPTQ-INT8 = 95.2%, AWQ-4bit = 93.7%, FP8 = 96.1%. Failures are mostly malformed tool args (strings where objects expected) or truncated arrays.

kevin_s: Example?

alex_m: Sure — baseline returns clean object:```json
{"tool":"search","args":{"query":"redwood inference quantization"}}
```
GPTQ output (one of many failure modes):```json
{"tool":"search","args":"{\"query\":\"redwood inference quantization\"}"}
```
So args became a JSON-encoded string instead of an object.

danielle: That explains a lot. Parser in app expects args to be an object and crashes on strict typing. Is it only when streaming or also non-streaming? :thinking:

alex_m: Both. We saw a slightly higher failure rate in streaming mode (likely chunk boundaries interacting with tokenization/decoder), but non-streaming still shows the stringified-JSON issues.

priya_r: Any pattern by prompt shape? function calls vs explicit "structured-output" prompts?

alex_m: Mostly function-call style prompts where we rely on model to emit a JSON structure for tool args. Prompts with explicit schema + examples (few-shot) reduce failure rates but quant variants still worse. Also more failures on long tool arg objects (more fields).

kevin_s: Hypothesis: quantized kernels / rounding change tokenization logits for characters like '{', '"', ':' causing the model to prefer emitting an escaped string for the JSON blob. Could also be temperature/decoding config sensitivity.

alex_m: Agreed. Quick ablation: we ran T=0.0 and temperature sweep. At T=0.0 failures reduced ~1-2% across quant variants but gap vs FP16 remained. Also tried forcing `stop` tokens and increased max_new_tokens — no real help.

eval-bot: Run summary written to /tmp/quant-schema-bakeoff/1769504321-summary.json

alex_m: Repro commands I used:```bash
python -m evals.run --model model-x --quant gptq --tests structured_function_calls --out /tmp/gptq_results.json
python -m evals.run --model model-x --quant awq --tests structured_function_calls --out /tmp/awq_results.json
```
Each run uses 5k prompts from our structured-calls corpus, schema validation via jsonschema strict mode.

danielle: Temporary mitigations we can ship: 1) post-process: if args is a string and looks like JSON, attempt json.loads; 2) add a small canonicalization layer that converts single-quoted keys, trailing commas, etc.; 3) route only safe traffic to quant variants until we fix model. Thoughts?

priya_r: Post-processing is OK as a stopgap but risky — ambiguous cases (string content that legitimately should be a string) might be misinterpreted. We should flag and add metrics for "postprocessed_true_positive" vs "postprocessed_false_positive".

kevin_s: From model side, options: 1) re-run quantization with per-channel calibration tweaks, 2) try AWQ with different block size, 3) GPTQ with more calibration samples, 4) experiment with mixed-precision (keep final layer fp16).

alex_m: I ran a quick AWQ block-size ablation: block 64 -> 93.7% valid, block 128 -> 94.9% valid. GPTQ with extra 5k calibration samples bumped it from 95.2 -> 96.4%. FP8 still fairly solid.

ops-ryan: For Dedicated deployment we should canary quant models with a header route (x-redwood-quant: awq) and 5-10% traffic only. For Hosted, default remains fp16. Add a circuit-breaker if JSON-valid-rate < 97% for 1min.

danielle: Agree. Also add a small strictness flag in Console per-route: "enforce_strict_schema" that fails request early (400) instead of letting the app crash, so we can surface the error to customers while we roll fixes.

alex_m: Next steps I propose: 1) Build a focused fuzzing job that mutates structured-tool-args prompts to exercise corner cases (escaped quotes, nested objects, long arrays). 2) Run per-quant variant calibration ablations (block size, calibration set size, keep-last-layers-fp16). 3) Add postproc parser-with-confidence metric and expose in Console. 4) Canary rollout + automatic fallback to FP16 when schema failure rate exceeds threshold.

priya_r: I can own the CI fuzz harness. Will add deterministic seeds and both streaming/non-streaming modes. Will also emit per-example diffs so we can inspect token-level causes. ETA: EOW for initial harness.

kevin_s: I'll re-run GPTQ with +10k calib samples and try mixed-precision final layer. Also will try AWQ block 128/256.

alex_m: Great. I'll draft a short runbook for SRE/ops with commands to roll back quant variants and how to interpret the JSON-valid-rate metric.

eval-bot: New task created: ML-2123 "Quant bakeoff: structured output fuzzing" assigned to priya_r, kevin_s, alex_m.

danielle: Thanks all. Please drop CI links and a couple failing examples in the ticket so we can prioritize. :thumbsup:
